topic: Mohe 1997 gravity anomaly — deep-attack of EXP-590 reframe (self-retraction lead)
our_argument_summary: Post-EXP-590, WIN-011 leads with a claimed 'self-retraction': Yang & Wang (2002) reanalyzed the same Mohe 1997 dataset and 'no significant anomaly during the very solar eclipse was found', characterized as the dome's own source withdrawing the -6.5 uGal number. The intermittency rebuttal is neutralized on that premise ('intermittency can never explain why one dataset stops showing a signal on reanalysis'). The kappa coupling is attacked as a cross-event cherry-pick validated against itself (BOU 2017 magnetic vs Mohe 1997 gravity, hardcoded ratio in monitor.py domain 7). Van Camp et al. (2001) four-SG null is demoted to corroboration. Verdict: Not Demonstrated.

holes_found.description: QUOTE-MINING IN OUR LEAD ARGUMENT. The EXP-590 reframe rests on calling Yang & Wang (2002) a 'self-retraction' ('The dome's own source withdrew the number', 'the dome's own cited value was withdrawn by its own author', detail_verdict_text 'was retracted by its own source author', tldr 'withdrawn by its own original author'). The verbatim quote is real, but the SAME abstract's next two sentences reaffirm the anomaly: 'However, there are two gravity anomaly valleys with near symmetrical decrease of about 6-7 uGal at the first contact and the last contact. This is the anomaly phenomenon observed and reported for the first time in the literature.' (Springer abstract, doi:10.1023/A:1021119023985, fetched this run). Yang & Wang 2002 did NOT withdraw the contact-phase valleys — it RELOCATED the null to the eclipse window proper and then used the data to constrain gravitational shielding. Our 'one dataset stops showing a signal on reanalysis' claim is false as stated. A dome defender who reads the publicly-visible abstract demolishes our lead in one screenshot — on the exact WIN where we lecture about source integrity. The intermittency-neutralization paragraph collapses with it, since it is built on the retraction premise.
holes_found.recommendation: Rebuild the lead on the dome's actual claim, which is STRONGER for us: the dome states '-6.5 uGal gravity anomaly AT ECLIPSE MAXIMUM' (raw-text/02-wins.txt:84). Both Wang 2000 and Yang & Wang 2002 report NO significant signal during the eclipse proper — the ~6-7 uGal valleys occur at first/last contact only. The dome's stated observable does not exist in its own source. This preserves every downstream beat: (a) intermittency cannot rescue a signal the source never reported at the claimed phase; (b) the kappa ratio pairs BOU-2017-at-maximum (-10.9 nT, raw-text/02-wins.txt:81) with a Mohe-at-maximum gravity value that is null in the source — the cherry-pick attack sharpens; (c) the contact-phase valleys that DO exist have a published conventional explanation co-authored by the same Yang (Van Flandern & Yang 2003, Phys. Rev. D 67, 022002, crossref-verified this run — atmospheric cooling/air-mass redistribution), which is the honest version of the 'the source walked it back' instinct. Keep verdict Not Demonstrated. Fields needing rewrite: detail_evidence paras 1-2, detail_verdict_text, tldr_evidence, tldr_verdict, finding.

holes_found.description: DEAD DOI + WRONG AUTHOR in published text. detail_evidence and the summary 'finding' attribute the four-SG 1999-eclipse null to 'Van Camp et al. (2001)' with doi:10.1023/A:1013940928637. That DOI does not exist: doi.org handle API returns responseCode 100 (handle not found; control DOI in same run resolved fine) and Crossref 404s it. The actual study is Mansinha, L., Ducarme, B., Hinderer, J., Meurers, B. & van Ruymbeke, M. (2001), 'Search for the Gravitational Absorption Effect Using Superconducting Gravimeters During the Eclipse of August 11, 1999', Journal of the Geodetic Society of Japan 47(1), 387-391 — NO DOI exists for it (OpenAlex W1212043147, verified this run). Van Camp is not an author; the name likely contaminated from the dome's own 'Van Camp 1999' Membach attribution (raw-text/02-wins.txt:89). Compounding: our c3 citation_check claimed this DOI 'VERIFIED this run' with the correct paper title — that verification was theater (the title is real, the DOI/author pairing was never checked against a resolver). Process flag for decider/tinker: a 'verified' entry in a prior citation_check was false.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace with: Mansinha et al. (2001, J. Geod. Soc. Japan 47(1), 387-391), link to J-STAGE (https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/sokuchi1954/47/1/47_1_387/_article) instead of a DOI. Update both detail_evidence and finding. The analyst should also re-verify the in-text quantitative details currently hung on this citation ('four superconducting gravimeters', '~1,000x more precise', 'above ~0.005 uGal') against the actual paper before re-publishing them, since they were sourced under the bogus verification.

stronger_arguments.description: Van Flandern & Yang (2003): the same Yang co-published a conventional explanation of the Mohe contact-phase valleys (atmospheric cooling / air-mass redistribution during eclipse shadow passage). This is the legitimate heir to the 'self-retraction' instinct — the source's co-author later endorsed a mundane cause — and it cannot be quote-mine-countered because it concedes the valleys are real.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome engages a real, published, genuinely contested strand of geophysics: Wang et al. (2000) is a bona fide Phys. Rev. D Rapid Communication (doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.62.041101, crossref-verified this run), and the two ~6-7 uGal contact-phase valleys it reported were reaffirmed, not withdrawn, by Yang & Wang (2002) (doi:10.1023/A:1021119023985 abstract, fetched this run). The Allais-effect literature remains formally open, and the dome is right that mainstream instruments were pointed at this question.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The dome's WIN needs a -6.5 uGal anomaly AT ECLIPSE MAXIMUM (raw-text/02-wins.txt:84), and that is the one phase where its own sources report null; the valleys that do exist sit at first/last contact with a published conventional explanation (doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.67.022002). No rule predicts when anomalies should appear, the value is literature-adopted not dome-derived (code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome=false, this review), and the kappa check consuming it is a hardcoded self-ratio (monitor.py:478, fetched this run). A real-but-conventionally-explained contact-phase signal demonstrates no dome-specific EM-gravitational coupling.

deeper_analysis: EXP-590 is a case study in an attractive framing outrunning its source. The analyst (and my own c3 — stronger_arguments[0] there proposed 'lead with the self-retraction') treated the 2002 abstract's first clause as a withdrawal without reading the 'However' that follows it. Three independent agents (analyst c3-c5 era, decider integration, my c5 carry-over note) repeated the framing without anyone re-opening the abstract; the c3 citation_check even logged the Van Camp DOI as verified-this-run when the DOI has never existed in the handle system. Both failures share a root cause: verification-by-recall instead of verification-by-resolver. Worth a tinker look at whether citation_check entries should require captured resolver output (HTTP code + returned title) rather than prose assertions. Strategic upside: the corrected attack (dome claims anomaly at maximum; source reports null at maximum; surviving valleys are contact-phase with a conventional explanation co-authored by the same Yang) is stronger, quote-mine-proof, and keeps every downstream element of EXP-590 — intermittency neutralization, cross-event cherry-pick, kappa circularity, Van Camp->Mansinha corroboration demotion — intact under repair. Verdict stays Not Demonstrated; this is an argument-integrity emergency, not a verdict emergency. ISS-2589 is closed and stays closed; these are fresh holes introduced/exposed by the EXP-590 integration, hence unresolved_prior_cycle=[].
